The placebo test actually backs up their claim more than I expected: 0.985 is the highest correlation across 3,464 windows since 1950, with only 6% exceeding 0.95 and nothing else hitting that level — so my instinct to dismiss "any rising line will correlate" doesn't hold up well here, though 2015-08 (0.971) and 1999-07 (0.976) come close enough to warrant a closer look.

The return correlation itself is weak (~0.03), confirming this is a shape-match (dip, rally, rollover) rather than a day-by-day match. I'm comparing historical analogs like 1987-10-19 (crash), Aug 2015 (only a ~12% correction before new highs), 1966 and 1957 (bear markets) — the top matches besides 2000 don't consistently predict a crash, so I should stick to what I've actually computed rather than overreach, and maybe pull forward 12-month drawdown/return stats for the best-matching windows to check this properly.

I also caught an error: I said the Nasdaq peaked in May 2026, but that's only true on a monthly-close basis — the actual daily intraday high was October 6, 2026. I need to fix that distinction in both my reply and the report, and add a section reviewing the overlay and the subsequent correction.
